title: The wire: lineage types
description: Part of the source of every type on the wire (#1135, #5380): one file per domain in Packages/Wire/schema. A $ref to another file names it (core.schema.json#/definitions/JSONValue); scripts/wire.sh gen reads them all.

LineageChanged.description: control/lineageChanged (#4276): a machine sent lineage the control plane's copy did not have, to the machine's person and to the admins: the changes of state it sent, so a client that shows working does not poll, and links when links changed too. Only refs, states and times.

links.description: Links started or ended too: a read of them is out of date.

LineageCost.description: What was banked under lineage nodes (#2350): a turn's cost, tokens and time, split evenly among the links active when it was banked. turns is a share of turns, so a turn on two nodes is half a turn on each.

limitTokens.description: Fresh input and output, as a limit counts them (#998).

workingSeconds.description: The agent, its tools and others at work.

LineageCostNode.description: One node's banked cost on a machine (#2350), whole, with what its rollups need: the repo or tracker its ref is in, the issues a PR fixes (ended links too: a PR closed without a merge still counts against its issue, as waste), the releases it is part of, and how a PR ended. A session's own cost is its turns that had no active link.

repo.description: The repo or tracker the node is in, as a ref (#4800): github:repo:#alexec/agents, linear:repo:#eng, or for a session its folder's repo (folder:repo:#<name> without one). Not a project (#3275).

partOf.description: The releases it is part of, by ref.

outcome.description: A PR's end: merged, closed (without a merge: waste) or reverted (a merged revert: waste). Absent while open. The list is open.

failedChecks.description: A PR's failed CI rounds: checks.failed, once per run and attempt.

firstAt.description: When the machine first banked or noted the node (#2351): the start of the work on it, for lead time.

startedAt.description: When work on an issue or PR started (#3562): its first works-on, opens or started link from a session, or for an issue the first PR that fixes it, whichever came first. Kept the earliest the machine saw, so it does not change when the links end.

level.description: An issue's level from its labels (#3562): epic, story, task, spike or bug. Kept once known, so a closed issue keeps it.

feature.description: An issue's feature: the name of its feature:<name> label (#3562).

parent.description: An issue's epic, by ref, as the forge's plan says it (#3562).

milestone.description: An issue's milestone, by name, as the forge's lists last said it (#4620). Kept once known, so a closed issue keeps it.

endedAt.description: When a PR ended (#2351): merged, closed or reverted. Absent while open.

resolved.description: An issue's or PR's title, state and labels as the machine's resolve cache has them (#3118), for reports/nodes. The machine asks no forge to fill it; absent until a lineage walk resolved the node.

sessions.description: The sessions linked to the node (works-on, opens, reviews), by ref, at most 20 (#3118).

estimate.description: An issue's estimate when its work started (#3561), kept once made, for the estimate against the actual when it closes.

forecast.description: An epic's first landing forecast (#4526), kept once made, for the forecast against when it lands.

files.description: A merged PR's files, by path, at most 100, as the forge said them when it merged (#4552), for the rework rate. Dropped 60 days after its merge.

reverts.description: The PR a merged revert reverts, by ref, from its body's "Reverts owner/repo#n" (#4552), for the recovery time.

openedAt.description: When a PR was opened (#4553): pr.opened's openedAt, the earliest kept. The approval wait's start when askedAt is unknown.

askedAt.description: When a PR was labelled needs-approval (#4553), from pr.labelled: the approval wait's start.

answeredAt.description: A PR's first answer by a person (#4553): the first pr.reviewed or pr.commented at or after the wait's start, while it was open, not by a bot and not a comment that starts with <!-- agent -->. The approval wait is this less askedAt, else openedAt.

ci.description: A PR's CI on its last head commit, from checks.passed and checks.failed (#4554), for CI time to green.

LineageCostRollup.description: lineage/cost (#2350): a node's cost rolled up. own is what was banked on the node itself. total adds its parts: an issue's PRs (the PRs that fix it); a release's PRs and the issues they fix; a repo's every node (kind repo, ref github:repo:#alexec/agents). waste is the parts' PRs closed without a merge or reverted. unlinked is the parts' sessions: turns with no active link. parts is the nodes added up, newest first, at most 500; limited says there are more.

LineageDelivery.description: A repo's delivery figures (#4552, epic #4551), from this machine's totals: the four DORA keys, DORA 2025's rework rate and flow efficiency, and CI time to green and failed rounds (#4554), over the windowDays (28) before at, each with a weekly series. A week is 7 days back from at, not a calendar week. A figure says how many it is made from; one made from none has no value. band is where a value falls among DORA 2024's clusters, a reference from teams of people, not a grade; rework rate, flow efficiency and the CI figures have none.

leadTime.description: Lead time for changes, in seconds: from the first work on an issue to the first release tag that carries a merged PR that fixes it; the median, and p90. Counted by the tag's time.

deploymentFrequency.description: Release tags a week (#3023), 0 for none, as is each week's; count is the tags.

changeFailureRate.description: Failures over merged PRs, 0 to 1, by merge time. A failure is a merged revert (a PR whose title starts with Revert), or a merged PR that fixes, by any lineage link, a priority:high bug filed within 7 days after a release tag in its repo. count is the merged PRs.

recoveryTime.description: Failed deployment recovery time, in seconds, the median: a revert's merge less the merge of the PR it reverts, or a fix's merge less its bug's filing. Counted by the recovery's merge.

reworkRate.description: DORA 2025's rework rate, 0 to 1: the share of merged PRs, of those with their files known, that change a file another PR merged in the 21 days before changed. count is the PRs with their files known.

flowEfficiency.description: The agents' working time on a closed issue and its PRs over its cycle time, at most 1, the median. Counted by its last merge.

approvalWait.description: The approval wait (#4553), in seconds: from a PR's needs-approval label (its opening when the label is unknown) to its first answer by a person; the median, and p90. Counted by the answer's time.

approvalShare.description: The share of merged PRs, 0 to 1, that waited for a person's answer before their merge (#4553), by merge time. count is the merged PRs.

ciTimeToGreen.description: CI time to green, in seconds (#4554): a merged PR's last push (the first run made on its last head commit) to the last of that commit's runs passing; the median, and p90. Counted by its merge. No band.

failedRounds.description: Failed CI rounds a merged PR, the mean (#4554): its checks.failed, once per run and attempt, 0 for none. count is the merged PRs. No band.

LineageDeliveryFigure.description: One delivery figure (#4552): value over the window, absent when made from none; p90 for lead time, the approval wait and CI time to green; count is what it is made from; weeks is the 4 weeks, oldest first; band is DORA 2024's.

band.description: elite, high, medium or low. The list is open.

LineageDeliveryWeek.description: A week of a delivery figure (#4552): the 7 days from since; value as the figure's, absent when made from none.

LineageEndRequest.description: lineage/end (#2348): the link from one node to another by this relationship stops being active now. Nothing is removed: the link keeps its start and gets an end.

LineageEstimate.description: lineage/estimate (#3559): what an issue or an epic will probably cost and take, from the closed issues like it on this machine (specs/3557-estimates/spec.md). An issue matches the closed issues with its type (bug or enhancement) and level (story, task, spike or bug); when fewer than 5 match, those with its type; then all of them (matchedBy says level, type or all). Only issues that closed with a merged PR that fixes them count, and no epic. Each figure is the median and the P10 to P90 range of the matches (8 in 10 like it land there), absent when fewer than 5 of them have it; with fewer than 5 closed issues in all there are no figures (closedIssues says how many there are). An epic adds up its open children by a simulation with a fixed seed: one match per child, 1,000 times. Its times follow its steps: the children of one step run at the same time, so a draw's time is the sum over the steps of its longest child. spent is what its closed children cost. landsAt is startAt (now when the request has none) plus the cycle time.

type.description: bug or enhancement, from its labels; absent with neither.

level.description: epic, story, task, spike or bug, from its labels; absent with none.

step.description: An epic's child's step in its plan (forge/plan).

closedIssues.description: The closed issues there are to match, on this machine.

matchedBy.description: An issue's rule: level (the same type and level), type or all. Absent for an epic, and with too few closed issues.

matches.description: The closed issues the estimate used; for an epic, those its open children used, each once.

leadTimeSeconds.description: From the first work to the last PR merged. It varies with the queue (lanes, CI, approvals), not with the work: the backtest's error was x2.4.

cycleTimeSeconds.description: From the start of work (#3562) to the last PR merged.

openChildren.description: An epic's children that are open.

closedChildren.description: An epic's children that are closed.

spent.description: What an epic's closed children cost, each with the PRs that fix it.

children.description: An epic's open children, each estimated as an issue, in step order.

kept.description: The estimate when work on it started (#3561), from the issues merged before then; absent before work starts. An issue's is kept in the cost store; an epic's is made from its plan's children, all open, at the epic's start.

actual.description: What a closed issue or epic took (#3561): an issue's own cost and its PRs'; an epic's, its own and every child's. Absent while open.

loaded.description: cost with the overhead loaded in (#4524), by currency: each figure times (1 + overhead.unlinkedRatio), and an epic's times (1 + overhead.epicRatio) too, as "direct $100, about $165 all in". Absent when cost is, or the overhead has no ratio.

overhead.description: The overhead that loaded is made with (#4524), on this machine.

LineageEstimateDates.description: When work lands (#3559): the median and the P10 to P90 range.

LineageEstimateKept.description: An estimate as it was when work started (#3561): lineage/estimate's figures, made from the closed issues that had merged before the start, so it can be set against what the work took when it closes. Dollars, output tokens and working seconds keep the median, and (#4525) the P10 and P90 beside it; the cycle time and the landing date keep the median and the P10 to P90 range, so Reports ▸ Value can say how often the range held the actual.

at.description: The start of work it was made for: the history is the issues merged before it.

matchedBy.description: level, type or all, as LineageEstimate.matchedBy; absent for an epic and with too few closed issues.

matches.description: The closed issues it was made from.

workingSeconds.description: The agents' time at work: the median.

workingSecondsP10.description: The agents' time at work: P10 (#4525).

workingSecondsP90.description: The agents' time at work: P90 (#4525).

cycleTimeSeconds.description: From the start of work to the last PR merged (#4525).

landsAt.description: When it was expected to land (#4525).

LineageEstimateRange.description: A figure's estimate (#3559): the median and the P10 to P90 range.

LineageEstimateRequest.description: lineage/estimate (#3559): an issue or an epic, and when work on it starts, for landsAt (now when absent).

LineageFigures.description: lineage/figures (#4427): a release's Lineage panel on its Work page, from this machine's totals; or (#4552) a repo's (kind repo, ref as LineageCostNode.repo), with its delivery figures. cost is its rollup's total, as lineage/cost's. sessions is how many sessions worked on it and its parts, each once; running is how many of them run now (starting, running or waiting on the person). runtimes is the runtimes of the sessions this machine has, the most sessions first. leadTimeSeconds is from the first work on its parts to its tag (#3878 removed the milestone figures). limited says the rollup had more parts than it counts. delivery is a repo's only. Another kind of node is refused.

LineageForecast.description: lineage/forecast (#4526; the method is specs/4533-forecasting/spec.md): what comes next, from this machine's totals. landings is the issues (not epics) that landed with a merged PR in the window of windowDays (14) before at, in the epic's repo when a node is asked for, else in every repo. milestone is the milestone asked for (#4620), whose landings are its repo's. lands is when the epic or the milestone lands; noForecast says why there is none (too little history, too few closed epics, nothing open). toComplete is the epic's estimate to complete, once three of its children closed with an estimate kept at their start. kept is the forecast kept on the epic's node, the first one made, so it can be scored when the epic lands. spend is what a week and a month cost at the window's pace, burn is each weekly allowance's pace, and serviceLevels is how long each level's issues took. Every figure says its window; a range is a probability, not a promise.

overhead.description: The overhead that toComplete.loaded and spend's loaded figures are made with (#4524).

assumes.description: The lanes and the runtime mix the window ran with (#4531).

whatIf.description: What the request's what-if moved (#4531); every figure is then the what-if's.

LineageForecastAssumes.description: What a forecast assumes (#4531): the lanes and the runtime mix of its window. lanes is the issues in flight (from their first work to their landing, or to now when open) in an average hour that had one; peakLanes is the most in any hour. runtimes is the mix, the most hours first.

LineageForecastBurn.description: A weekly allowance's pace (#4526): used (0 to 1) at its last reading at, of the week that resets at resetsAt. runsOutAt is when it runs out at that pace, absent when it lasts to the reset (lasts).

LineageForecastKept.description: An epic's landing forecast as it was made (#4526), kept once on its node, so it can be scored when the epic lands: the P50 and P85 dates, the window, the share and the open children then.

LineageForecastLands.description: When an epic lands (#4526, method H of specs/4533-forecasting/spec.md): a Monte Carlo of 1,000 draws with a fixed seed, each resampling hours of the window and keeping each landing in an hour with the chance share, until the open children are done. p50 and p85 are dates. share is the median share of the folder's landings that the closed epics had over their lives, from groups of them. open and closed are the children as the plan says now, with no growth for children not filed yet; stepsLeft is the blocked-by steps of the open ones, as context only: they do not enter the dates. For a milestone (#4620), open and closed are its items in the store, the share is the closed milestones', stepsLeft is 0, and growing says that less than half of its items have landed, so its scope is still growing (a milestone grows about 5× after its first issue): the dates are a floor.

LineageForecastRequest.description: lineage/forecast (#4526): an epic, for when it lands and its estimate to complete; or a milestone (#4620), by name, for when it lands, in folder's repo (any repo without one); without either, only the spend, the burn and the service levels, over every repo. whatIf (#4531) asks for the same figures with another lane limit or runtime mix; a what-if forecast is never kept.

milestone.description: A milestone's name (#4620): its items are the store's issues in it. Not with node.

folder.description: The folder whose repo the milestone is in.

LineageForecastRuntime.description: A runtime's part of a forecast's window (#4531), from this machine's usage and time histories: share is its part of the agents' working hours (the agent, its tools and others), hours is those hours, and rate is its cost per working hour.

LineageForecastServiceLevel.description: How long a level's issues took (#4526): of the closed issues of the level that landed in the window, half took up to p50Seconds and 85% up to p85Seconds, from the start of work to the last PR merged. Only a level with five or more.

LineageForecastSpend.description: What a week and a month cost at the window's pace (#4526): dollars by currency, P10 to P90, from 1,000 draws of 7 and 30 of the window's days. A day's cost is what the issues that landed on it took, all of their work, so it follows the landings, not the hour the money went.

loadedWeek.description: week with the overhead loaded in (#4524): times (1 + overhead.unlinkedRatio). Absent with no ratio.

LineageForecastToComplete.description: An epic's estimate to complete (#4526): dollars by currency, P10 to P90, for its open children and the lead. Each child's estimate is drawn from its matches and scaled by one factor per draw, shared by every child, lognormal from the closed children's actual over their kept estimate (ratio is its median, from closed of them). The lead's term is the epic's own cost over its closed children's, leadRatio, times the children's.

loaded.description: cost with the overhead loaded in (#4524): times (1 + overhead.unlinkedRatio). The lead is in cost already, so not the epic ratio. Absent with no ratio.

LineageForecastWhatIf.description: A what-if for lineage/forecast (#4531): lanes is a lane limit (below 1 is as the window ran), and mix is a runtime mix, each runtime's share of the working hours, scaled to add up to 1. Absent, each is as the window ran.

LineageForecastWhatIfEffect.description: What a what-if moved (#4531). A lane limit keeps, in each hour of the window, min(in flight, lanes) / in flight of its landings, so the dates move out and a week's spend falls; a limit at or above peakLanes moves nothing, as no hour ran more. pace is the landings it keeps over the window's. A mix moves the dollars only: cost is the mix's cost per working hour over the window's, and each allowance's pace moves by its runtime's share over the window's. Landings do not say their runtime, so a mix does not move the dates.

mix.description: By runtime id, scaled to add up to 1.

LineageGraph.description: lineage/walk (#2348): the nodes the walk reached and the links it went along. limited says the walk stopped at its limit on nodes, so there is more. resolved is each node's title, state and labels from its connector, by ref, for the nodes a connector could resolve (#3089). resolving says some nodes are still being resolved in the background, so walk again shortly for them (#3102). states is the current state of each session node in it that has one, by ref (#4274).

LineageLink.description: A typed link in the lineage graph (#2348): from works-on, opens, fixes, started, reviews, closes or part-of to. source is how the host knows it: start, branch, pr-body, helper, agent, person or forge. at is when it started; endedAt is set when it stops being active (a PR merged, a session archived). Both lists are open: a host keeps a relationship or a source it does not know.

LineageLinkRequest.description: lineage/link (#2348): start a link. When the same link is active already, it is the answer, unchanged.

LineageLinks.description: The links of a node, newest first (#2348), or the links lineage/end ended. limited says there are more than the answer holds. states is a session node's changes of state, newest first, so the first is its state now (#4274); absent for a node that is not a session, or a session with none recorded.

LineageNode.description: A node in the lineage graph (#2348). kind is what it is: issue, pr, session, workflow-run, commit, file, branch or release, and the list is open. ref names it apart from any tracker, in the full ref form provider:type:topic#id (#4800): github:issue:alexec/agents#123, gitlab:mr:group/repo#45, linear:issue:eng#ENG-4, jira:issue:abc#ABC-9, agents:session:alexec/agents#<agent id>. A reader takes the old form (<scheme>:<id>, as github:alexec/Agents#123 or session:<agent id>) for one release.

LineageNodeRequest.description: lineage/links and lineage/walk (#2348): a node, and for a walk how many links away to go (1 to 4; 2 when not said: issue, sessions, PRs).

LineageOverhead.description: The overhead (#4524): the cost no issue, PR or release carries, over the nodes that last changed in the last windowDays days (a rolling 14). unlinked is the sessions' cost that went on no work (a Scrum Master's turn that started nothing, a review, a check); linked is the cost on issues, PRs and releases. unlinkedRatio is unlinked over linked, and epicRatio is the epics' own cost (their leads') over their children's and their PRs', each in currency, the currency with the most linked cost; absent when there is nothing to divide by. A loaded figure is a direct one times (1 + unlinkedRatio), and an epic's plan times (1 + epicRatio) too. uncounted names what no figure has.

currency.description: The currency of the ratios; absent with no linked cost.

uncounted.description: What no figure here counts: people-time (a person's reviews and answers) and ci-minutes (the forge's runners).

LineagePRCI.description: A PR's CI on its last head commit (#4554): headSha is that commit; pushedAt is when its first run was made, by the push (a rerun keeps it); greenAt is when the last of its runs that passed finished, absent until one passed. A new head commit starts it again.

LineageResolved.description: A node's title, state and labels from its connector (#3089), resolved and cached on the daemon so a lineage renderer shows "Fix flaky test" rather than its ref. state is open, closed or merged (a pull request's; an issue's is open or closed); absent when the connector does not say. labels is empty when it has none. Resolved for a GitHub or GitLab issue or pull request only; Linear and releases are not resolved yet.

createdAt.description: When the forge says the issue or PR was made (#4552): a bug's filing, for the change failure rate.

LineageRuntimeCount.description: A runtime of lineage/figures' sessions, and how many of them it ran (#4427).

LineageSessionIssue.description: One heading of a search for an epic (#3900): the epic or one of its sub-issues, and its title, absent while the host has not resolved it.

LineageSessionMatch.description: A session on the issue, and the issue it is on: the one asked for, or one of its sub-issues. A session on a PR is on the issue the PR fixes.

LineageSessionOn.description: A session that lineage links to one or more of the nodes asked for (#4276), on any machine in the scope: the session's node, its machine, the nodes asked for it is linked to, when its first link to them started, and its state now when its machine sent one.

host.description: The id of the machine that sent the link.

LineageSessionState.description: A change of a session node's state, as its machine recorded it (#4274): state is what it changed to, at is when. The machine keeps the changes of the last 90 days, and each session's latest whatever its age.

LineageSessionStateName.description: A session's state in lineage (#4274): working is in a turn (or starting one); waiting waits on an event, CI, a timer or a place to start; needs-you waits on a person, for a question or an approval; stopped is not running and not archived; archived is archived; deleted is deleted, and the node keeps no title. A state this build does not know reads as stopped.

LineageSessions.description: The sessions on this machine that lineage links to the issue, to its sub-issues or to their PRs, each once, on the first issue in issues they came by. limited says there were more sub-issues or sessions than are counted.

issues.description: The issue asked for, then its sub-issues in the epic's order (#3900), each once, with its title when the host has it: the headings a search for an epic groups its sessions under. Only the issue asked for when it has no sub-issues; absent from a host too old to say.

LineageSessionsOn.description: lineage/sessionsOn (#4276): the sessions linked to the nodes asked for, each once, the earliest link first. limited says there were more than lineage's answer bound (500).

LineageSessionsOnRequest.description: lineage/sessionsOn (#4276): the nodes (at most 500, such as an epic and its children) whose sessions to say, over every machine's copy that the scope takes. The scope is as reports/value's: me when absent for a member, the organisation for an admin.

LineageSessionsRequest.description: lineage/sessions (#3899): a session search for #<number> asks for the sessions on that issue, on the issues part-of it (its sub-issues, at most 100) and on the PRs that fix them. The issue is #<number> in the forge repo of each of this machine's folders.

LineageStateChange.description: A session node's change of state, and when (#4275), as lineage/sync sends it. Only the ref, the state and the time: no title or text (principle 7).

LineageSync.description: lineage/sync (#4275): what changed in a machine's lineage since its last send: links started or ended (each whole, as the machine has it now), and its sessions' changes of state (#4274). reset starts the control plane's copy of the links again from this send, the first of a whole send; the states are kept.

LineageSyncAnswer.description: lineage/sync's answer (#4275). full: the control plane has no copy of this machine's links (a new or moved control plane), so the machine sends them all again, the first with reset.

LineageWalkAllRequest.description: lineage/walkAll (#4276): lineage/walk over the control plane's merged copy, every machine's links that the scope takes, so a machine that sleeps is still in it. depth is as lineage/walk's; the scope is as reports/value's. The answer has no resolved: the control plane keeps no titles (principle 7).
